title: Corridor Factor Table for Universal Life Insurance
content:
The corridor factor is the minimum ratio of the death benefit to the account value under the guideline premium test for Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance. The same table applies to all six tiers, from the Ashgrove Lifetime Guarantee UL to the Ashgrove Indexed UL Premier.

## Table

| Insured's attained age from | Corridor factor |
|---|---|
| 0 | 2.50 |
| 41 | 2.43 |
| 45 | 2.15 |
| 50 | 1.85 |
| 55 | 1.50 |
| 60 | 1.30 |
| 65 | 1.20 |
| 70 | 1.15 |
| 75 | 1.05 |
| 91 | 1.04 |
| 92 | 1.03 |
| 93 | 1.02 |
| 94 | 1.01 |
| 95 | 1.00 |

## Rule of reading

The factor that applies is the one for the highest listed attained age that is not above the insured's attained age. Each row therefore runs up to the age before the next listed age: 2.43 applies at ages 41 through 44, 1.05 at ages 75 through 90, and 1.00 from age 95 on.

## Hypothetical readings

| Insured's attained age | Factor |
|---|---|
| 40 | 2.50 |
| 44 | 2.43 |
| 63 | 1.30 |
| 90 | 1.05 |
| 91 | 1.04 |
| 99 | 1.00 |

An account value of $200000.00 at attained age 63 corresponds to a corridor amount of 1.30 times $200000.00, which is $260000.00.
